# Acid stress varies by copper producer; ICSG forecasts a near-term refined surplus

## Signal

Verification follow-up to the already processed October 25 bookmarks. Material delta from prior card(s): 005; new producer counterevidence and primary forecast/curtailment checks.

## Data

Jubilee's [September 14 issuer update](https://www.ukwire.co.uk/announcement/rns/jubilee-metals-group--jlp/fy2026-production-and-operational-update-/9769108) places acid costs >200% higher and Sable disruption in **April–June fiscal Q4**, with no national affected-tonnage estimate. [First Quantum's July 28 Q2 results](https://www.first-quantum.com/news/first-quantum-minerals-reports-second-quarter-2026-results/) record Kansanshi selling about **36kt of acid/$12m** to third parties in that same quarter. Producer exposure differs.

[ICSG October 14 forecast](https://icsg.org/download/2026-10-14-press-release-icsg-copper-market-forecast-2026-2027/), two pages read, projects refined surpluses **104kt in 2026 / 368kt in 2027**. It warns about Middle East disruptions and unreported Chinese stocks. [IEA's 2026 outlook](https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2026/executive-summary) estimates a **25% 2035 project-pipeline gap** on a different horizon/basis. BNEF's exact bookmarked 8%/44% forecasts remain gated/unverified. None is an observed current deficit.

[Mosaic Q2 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1285785/000128578526000112/mos-20260630.htm), operating sections read, links sulfur/supply pressure with temporary phosphate/Brazil curtailments. FERT already covers Mosaic cuts (KB-FERT-075/081); this is primary corroboration, not a new sector event. Specific plant utilization claims were not verified here.

## Relevance

**MIDAS ACTION:** incorporate the same-quarter acid counterexample and separate near-term refined balance from long-term mine capacity. **FERT ACTION:** fold primary corroboration into existing phosphate evidence; no blanket fertilizer-shortage inference. VULCAN/WATT receive conditional input-cost context, CARL food-cost transmission. Owner grades remain yours.

# Current ensembles support vortex weakening; reversal and surface cold remain uncertain

## Signal

Verification follow-up to the already processed October 25 bookmarks. Material delta from prior card(s): 008; current ensemble comparison replaces single-run-only evidence.

## Data

[Current original-processing graphic](https://scorvec.com/assets/sst/nh_vortex.webp), inspected in full, includes runs through **October 25 12Z**; [method](https://scorvec.com/stratosphere.html) uses ECMWF/NOAA/ECCC open data. Ensemble means at 10hPa/60°N weaken from about 22m/s toward roughly 0–4m/s in early November. Its **67%** annotation refers to GEPS members crossing easterly on some day within 15 days. That is one model's member fraction, not calibrated multi-model probability. IFS/AIFS/GEFS means remain weakly westerly; analysis remains westerly.

This improves on the October 23 single deterministic run. Official ECMWF chart access was blocked, so the recovered current comparison is independently processed open data. A purported latest OU GEFS chart was excluded because its image was dated August 14, 2025.

Thus the two figures can be valid under different explicitly named definitions. Full historical quarterly series was not reconstructed: **“first ever negative” remains unverified**. This is numerical reconciliation, not independent evidence of a fresh capex cut or funding failure.

# NY Fed data contradict the graduate-unemployment “45-year first”; Q2 figures remain supported

## Signal

Verification follow-up to the already processed October 25 bookmarks. Material delta from prior card(s): 014 and BM-02 item36; source-quarter ambiguity resolved and primary historical counterexample calculated.

## Data

[NY Fed current page](https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market), body/methodology read October 25, confirms **2026 Q2 recent-graduate unemployment 5.6%, underemployment 42%**. Underemployment concerns employed graduates in jobs typically not requiring degrees; it is not an unemployment add-on.

The page's legacy XLS link is a July 2023 underemployment-job-type workbook, so it cannot establish the current unemployment history. Current chart JavaScript yields this [primary CSV](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/research/interactives/data/college-labor-market/college-labor-unemployment-data.csv), January 1990–June 2026, parsed in full. It contains **73 monthly observations before 2025** with recent-graduate unemployment above all workers. Q2 2019 averages **3.957% recent graduates vs 3.557% all workers**. This is a quarterly counterexample too.

The attached 2025 graphic's “first in 45 years” comparison therefore fails on NY Fed's current basis. This does not negate current graduate weakness, reconcile all historical vintages or demonstrate AI displacement. Original014 explicitly left the historical claim unverified; this is a verification update, not withdrawal of a previously certified claim.

## Relevance

**LABOR ACTION:** exclude the first-ever framing and retain the dated Q2 observations/definitions when assessing the existing low-hire picture. CARL/HENRY receive household-demand context, no causal estimate.
